security_audit.summary: Most static external-command alerts are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, package names, and code fences rather than Ruby or shell backtick execution. The real risks are the broad Bash(belt *) permission, remote Python execution through inference.sh, and sample code that performs outbound HTTP requests. No prompt injection language was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.suggestion: Limit allowed tools to the exact belt app run command and variants needed for infsh/python-executor, or require confirmation for all belt commands.
Add a clear warning that code, inputs, outputs, and network requests are processed by inference.sh outside the local workspace.
Add guidance to avoid secrets in HTTP requests and to get user approval before scraping websites or calling external APIs.
Consider an allowlist note or scanner metadata so documentation formatting is not confused with executable backtick syntax.

content.user_title: Run Python Code in a Sandbox
content.value_statement: AI assistants often need a controlled place to run Python tasks without local setup. This skill sends Python code to inference.sh and returns console output and generated files.
actual_capabilities: Runs Python 3.10 code through the inference.sh belt CLI.
Uses common libraries for data analysis, plotting, scraping, media, PDFs, and 3D files.
Returns console output from scripts when output capture is enabled.
Returns files written under the output folder.
Supports timeout, working directory, capture output, and high memory variants.
limitations: Requires an inference.sh account and belt CLI login.
Runs on CPU only, so GPU workloads and large ML training are not supported.
Executes non-interactive scripts; visual results should be saved as files.
Can make outbound network requests from example code, so sensitive data needs care.

use_cases.title: Analyze and Visualize Data
use_cases.description: Run Python scripts that summarize datasets and return charts or tables.

use_cases.title: Automate One-Off Tasks
use_cases.description: Execute short scripts for file conversion, data cleanup, and repeatable workflow steps.

use_cases.title: Generate Media and Documents
use_cases.description: Create images, videos, PDFs, and 3D assets using installed Python libraries.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Simple Script
prompt_templates.prompt: Use python-executor to run a short Python script that prints a calculation result and explain the output.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Data Chart
prompt_templates.prompt: Use python-executor to analyze this small dataset, summarize the key numbers, and return a chart file.

prompt_templates.title: Process Uploaded Assets
prompt_templates.prompt: Use python-executor to resize these images, save optimized copies in the output folder, and report the new dimensions.

prompt_templates.title: Build an Automated Data Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Use python-executor to fetch approved public data, clean it, create summary tables, and return charts plus a brief method note.

output_examples.input: A user asks for sales totals and a bar chart from a small table.
output_examples.output: The assistant returns totals by category and attaches a chart image generated by the sandbox.

output_examples.input: A user asks to resize a set of product images.
output_examples.output: The assistant returns optimized image files and a short report with new dimensions.

output_examples.input: A developer asks to inspect a public API response.
output_examples.output: The assistant summarizes the returned fields and notes any request errors or rate limits.

best_practices: Review code before execution when it handles credentials, private files, or customer data.
Set realistic timeouts and use the high memory variant only for larger workloads.
Save artifacts in the output folder when you need charts, media, documents, or data files.
anti_patterns: Do not send secrets or regulated data unless the external execution environment is approved.
Do not use it for interactive notebooks, graphical windows, or long-running services.
Do not rely on the sandbox for GPU training or production hosting.

faq.question: Does this run code on my local machine?
faq.answer: No. The skill uses the inference.sh service through the belt CLI.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: It is declared for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can it access the internet?
faq.answer: The examples show HTTP requests, so review network use before running sensitive tasks.

faq.question: How are generated files returned?
faq.answer: Files saved in the output folder are detected and returned with the result.

faq.question: Does it support GPU workloads?
faq.answer: No. The documented environment is CPU only.

faq.question: What should I check before publishing this skill?
faq.answer: Confirm external service terms, data handling, and narrow CLI permissions for belt commands.
